subject: Re: Post-call: PII handling for prompts/outputs (BrightPath)
messages:
From: Alice Johnson <alice.j@brightpath.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@brightpath.com>
Date: 2028-03-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: PII handling for prompts/outputs

Thanks for the call this morning, Rishi  good overview. A couple quick clarification asks from our security/compliance team about what happens to prompts and model outputs when we use Redwood's hosted API:  

1) Exactly what is retained by default (prompts, outputs, metadata)?
2) Where is that data stored (region/residency)?
3) For how long is it retained, and what controls do we have to reduce retention (or disable persistence entirely)?
4) Is any of that content used to train models or for model improvements?

We'd also like a short written confirmation we can share internally and with our procurement team. Can you send a brief summary and any links to the DPA / SOC 2 evidence?

Cheers,
Alice
Alice Johnson
Head of Product Security, BrightPath Health

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.j@brightpath.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-30T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: PII handling for prompts/outputs

Alice F thanks for the list, and great meeting earlier. Short answers here; attaching a 11page summary and DPA draft for your procurement team.

1) What is retained by default?
- Hosted (Redwood API): by default we retain request metadata (timestamps, model id, latency, token counts) and request/response payloads (full prompts & outputs) for up to 30 days for debugging, security investigations, and billing reconciliation.
- Dedicated: logs and payloads are retained only if the customer enables logging; retention period is customer-configurable (we recommend 30 days).
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Redwood control plane does not persist customer prompts/outputs; storage and logs remain in the customer environment.

2) Where is data stored?
- Hosted: stored in the region you select for your account (we support US & EU regions today). For BrightPath we've confirmed US residency (us-east-1).
- Dedicated/Private: data residency follows the customer's infra.

3) Retention & controls:
- Default hosted retention is 30 days for payloads. Customers can:  
  a) Enable "do-not-store" at the account or per-request level (X-Redwood-Do-Not-Store header) which prevents persistence of prompt/output payloads.  
  b) Request shorter retention or enabled automatic deletion via the account settings.  
- We also provide a retention policy export and one-click purge for enterprise accounts as part of the onboarding flow.

4) Training use:
- We do NOT use customer prompts/outputs to train our public models. Customer data is not included in model training. Reducing or disabling storage via "do-not-store" ensures no payloads are persisted.

I've copied Neha (Security & Compliance) and Marissa (Customer Success) to confirm the wording and attach our SOC 2 reference. Let me know if you want a signed DPA and a short attestation we can send for procurement.

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Alice Johnson <alice.j@brightpath.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-30T11:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: PII handling for prompts/outputs

Adding a couple of compliance specifics for procurement:  

- Hosted retention specifics: request/response payloads (prompts & outputs) are retained for 30 days by default; request metadata and audit logs are kept for 365 days.  
- Deletion/opt-out: account-level "Do Not Store" disables persistence of payloads on our hosted service; when enabled, only metadata (request id, timestamp, token counts, model id) is retained for billing and SRE purposes. We also support per-request header X-Redwood-Do-Not-Store and an API flag when creating sessions.
- Training: confirmed — we do not use customer payloads to train public models. We may use aggregated telemetry (non-PII) for runtime performance improvements; that data is behavioral/aggregate only.
- Residency: data for BrightPath hosted accounts will remain in US region (us-east-1). For EU customers we store EU-region data only.
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II report is available under NDA; our DPA includes clauses for deletion, breach notification (72 hours), and subprocessors. I've attached the DPA draft and a short customer attestation template you can include with your procurement docs.

Marissa F can CS follow up with onboarding steps to enable the Do Not Store setting if BrightPath requests it?

-Neha
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Alice Johnson <alice.j@brightpath.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Thanks F this is exactly what we needed. Two quick asks before we close:  
1) Can you send a one-paragraph attestation we can drop into our vendor security review that states "By default Redwood retains prompts/outputs for 30 days in the selected region; customers can enable Do Not Store to disable persistence; customer content is not used to train Redwood public models."  
2) Please attach the DPA and the SOC 2 contact (or the NDA link) so procurement can pull the report.

If you can have those over today, procurement will be able to move the contract draft to legal. Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Alice
